axis_coverage.assessment: Discovery is 914 whitespace-delimited words, within 700–1000. Four items; two named navigable implementation leads; one dated version lead; compact comparison; exactly three numbered prospective checks; uncertainty and bounded next step. Scope remains one-user chunking/identity/encryption; no scheduling, UI, full restore architecture, universal winner or cross-user feature requirement. Full map, fixture and common assignment read; corpus is null. Reported seven primary sources span at least Restic, Borg and USENIX, satisfying three-source/two-project minimum. Eight listed attempts including failure are consistent with candidate page cap, but absent full retrieval trace prevents certifying actual attempt count.

Fixed offsets, Rabin rolling CDC, Gear/FastCDC and secret-seeded Buzhash differ in boundary mechanism or optimization/security approach. Fixed is useful as the same-length-overwrite/control baseline; insertion failure is explicit. Ciphertext identity is separated from boundary identity, and conventional convergent encryption is discussed as an optional background alternative with guessability risk. No exhaustive-algorithm survey is required by this bounded four-item brief.

Restic window and binary units are accurate for the cited documentation; the unsplit-small-file exception is not needed to adopt a product default and no default is adopted. FastCDC speed/ratio is scoped to authors’ benchmarks. Seeded boundaries are not presented as cryptographic proof, visible stored sizes remain, and the preprint is construction/threat-model specific. Password wrapping, content/master-key changes, ID changes and compromise revocation are distinguished. HMAC+random-nonce AEAD is explicitly a design inference. Kopia example version is not treated as current/default. MLE determinism needs the narrow non-material wording limitation L1.

Restic/chunker and Borg source URLs are real and inspectable; reviewer independently opened their public project pages, including chunker.go and src/borg listings. Candidate correctly says code was not opened/audited. Restic v0.18.1 expressly dates pack randomization mitigation to 0.18.0. This is a useful history/version lead, not a deployment or attack validation claim.

The comparison addresses upload reuse after inserts, CPU/ratio/compatibility and visible equality/sizes. Key wrapping versus actual rotation and old-version recoverability are a useful product distinction. Workload, edit distribution, leakage tolerance and key-change semantics remain genuine external product decisions. No winner is chosen; the two-leading-candidate next step is prospective, not a hidden adoption decision.

Evidence supports retaining fixed as control and investigating CDC; no blanket rejection of CDC from the attack paper or extrapolation of a speed guarantee occurs. Cross-user sharing is not promoted into scope. Not requiring convergent encryption for one-user reuse is justified by independently keyed identity/randomized encryption. Restic mitigation and key-change distinctions remain in the output. No draft/critique/final chain or critique dispositions were supplied; those obligations are NOT_APPLICABLE rather than guessed passes.

Front insertion, overwrite and middle edit compare actual reuse/CPU/upload at similar chunk sizes; a synthetic store-observer exercise targets leakage and guessed-content confirmation; disposable key-change tests distinguish wrapping/rotation and check old restores/credentials/rewrite volume. Candidate explicitly reports zero local implementation, benchmark, restore or rotation tests. Opened documentation is not an executable oracle. No nonexistent deployed service or whole-product test was required.
